numerical_failure.observed_behavior: With method='homomorphic', the homomorphic mask construction is backwards: the check for even signal length is inverted, which generates a ripple in the bandpass of the resulting minimum phase filter (visible in the magnitude response, more easily seen with float32).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The magnitude response of the minimum phase filter should match the expected result without bandpass ripple; the Nyquist bin of the mask should be set to 1 when n_fft is even and 2 when n_fft is odd (win[stop] = 1 + (n_fft % 2)).

category_specific_evidence: The PR body states the ripple is more easily seen with float32, and the test is parametrized over float32 and float64.

The fix changes the Nyquist-bin weighting in the homomorphic minimum_phase cepstral window: win[0]=1, win[1:stop]=2, and the Nyquist bin at stop = n_fft//2 is set to 1 + (n_fft % 2), replacing the previous odd-only Nyquist assignment.
The fix also creates win with dtype=h_temp.dtype and uses xp.real(h_temp) instead of h_temp.real.
The regression test test_nyquist uses N in (963, 964), an odd and an even filter length, and fc=10 with fs=100 and a hann-window firwin lowpass filter.
The reproducer from issue #22752 uses N=963, fc=0.13655297795265942 Hz, a Hamming window, and minimum_phase(h, method='homomorphic', n_fft=N, half=False).
The PR author states the atol values were chosen empirically on their hardware and may need tweaking for CI.
reproduction_risks: The PR states the atol values were chosen empirically on the author's hardware and may need adjustment for CI, so no numeric tolerance is given in the passages.
The issue reproducer depends on torch and matplotlib and was reduced in the PR to a version without torch; the minimal numeric test body is truncated in the passages after fc = 10.
The expected numerical values of the minimum-phase output or the violated spectral property (magnitude response equality) are not stated explicitly in the passages.
